newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures close sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures close sharply lower.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures closed sharply lower after briefly trimming losses when the sell-off in U.S. bonds and stocks dragged down the dollar, traders and analysts said.
However, some analysts said expectations for continued dollar weakness were overdone, especially amid signs of strong U.S. economic growth.
"You still have strong U.S. growth and that will be positive for the dollar," Michael Malpede, senior currency analyst, said.

The U.S. March international trade deficit shrank more than 19 percent to $8.51 billion, compared to average trade estimates of $10.3 billion and against February's deficit which was upwardly revised to $10.54 billion.

June yen, marks, Swiss francs and sterling expanded opening declines on the data, and continued to inch steadily lower throughout the day. Even Canadian dollars, which opened higher, turned slightly lower.
U.S. Commerce Undersecretary Everett Ehrlich said recent economic numbers, including the trade data, pointed to first-quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of six percent.
According to original reports, GDP rose 5.6 percent, its fastest pace in more than five years.

Continued signs of strong economic growth, coupled with nervousness about the fate of European economic and monetary union (EMU), will push June marks and Swiss francs towards their one-week lows in the near term, Malpede said.
He is looking for dollar/mark to rise to 1.71 spot, or about $0.5859 in June, and dollar/Swiss franc to climb to 1.44 spot, or roughly $0.6965 in June, by the end of next week.
"I don't think it's a straight trend down for the dollar," Malpede said. Both June marks and June Swiss francs managed to hold above Tuesday's overall low.
Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Koebnick said on Wednesday that it would be better to allow Germany some leeway in meeting the criteria for EMU than to delay its start.

Koebnick said Bonn's plan to revalue the Bundesbank's gold and currency reserves was unfortunately timed because it coincided with news of an 18-billion mark tax revenue shortfall. Some traders expressed concern in general with Germany's revaluation plan.
Declines in Swiss franc futures were attributed to the Swiss National Bank's (SNB) statement that it added liquidity to the money market.
Even yen futures, which are viewed more bullishly than marks or Swiss francs, are expected to dip to $0.008690, or 115.50 spot, in the short-term, some traders said.

At the end of pit trade, June yen was off $0.000117 at $0.008787, marks off $0.0053 at $0.5909, Swiss francs off $0.0108 at $0.7119, sterling off $0.0134 at $1.6424, Can dollars flat at $0.7328 and Aussie dollars up $0.0130 at $0.7869.
